assets.description: Customer account data including email addresses, passwords, and delivery addresses stored in the database
Customer order history records stored in the database
Transaction records kept by the shop for each card payment
Product catalogue managed through the administration interface
Administration interface used by staff to manage products and view orders
Third-party payment provider integration handling card payments

vulnerabilities.description: Customer passwords may be stored without adequate hashing, making them recoverable if the database is compromised.
The customer account registration and login forms may be susceptible to credential stuffing or brute-force attacks.
The database storing customer accounts and order history may lack sufficient access controls, exposing data to unauthorised queries.
Transaction records may contain sensitive payment metadata that could be exposed through insecure storage or access controls.
The administration interface may lack multi-factor authentication, making it vulnerable to unauthorised staff account takeover.
The administration interface may be exposed to the internet without adequate network restrictions, broadening the attack surface.
The integration with the third-party payment provider may use insecure or misconfigured API credentials that could be intercepted or misused.
The product catalogue may be modifiable without sufficient input validation, enabling injection of malicious content.

threats.description: An external attacker exploits a weak or reused password to gain access to a customer account and steal personal and delivery information.
An external attacker performs a SQL injection attack against the database to extract all customer account records including email addresses and hashed passwords.
An external attacker queries the database through a vulnerable endpoint to access customer order history in bulk.
A malicious insider with database access exfiltrates transaction records to sell or misuse payment metadata.
An external attacker compromises staff credentials and logs into the administration interface to tamper with the product catalogue.
A malicious staff member abuses their legitimate access to the administration interface to view or export customer order data without authorisation.
An external attacker intercepts or steals the API credentials used to communicate with the third-party payment provider and uses them to disrupt or manipulate payment processing.
An external attacker injects malicious content into the product catalogue through the administration interface to conduct a supply-chain or cross-site scripting attack against customers.
A staff member accidentally deletes or corrupts product catalogue entries while using the administration interface, causing loss of data.
